text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying those symptoms. Given the flank pain and fever following antibiotic treatment, I need to check for signs of infection in the urine. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia: Present, Bacterial Culture: Negative, Cytospin Stained With Hansel’s Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of binucleated eosinophils in the urine, combined with your history of a rash after antibiotic use, strongly suggests an allergic reaction rather than an infection. Do you currently have any visible skin rash or itching?

speaker: Patient
text: The sinus symptoms improved, but the flank pain and fever stayed. The rash happened during the antibiotics and then resolved after the change in medication.

speaker: Doctor
text: The eosinophilic cystitis and history of drug-induced rash strongly point to acute interstitial nephritis rather than a bacterial infection. I have enough evidence to finalize the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
